title: 3. Distribution, Supply Chain & Unit Economics
book_title: Chapter 3: How It Is Sold & Delivered — Distribution & Unit Economics

epigraph.quote: Culture eats lateral hiring for breakfast; an Account Manager groomed inside our math stays for a decade.
epigraph.author: Anand Rathi Wealth Management Philosophy (Investor Disclosures)

web_blocks.html: Banks often cross-sell wealth products through high-churn branch managers, while boutique firms poach senior bankers with guaranteed signing bonuses. Anand Rathi Wealth instead operates a hub-and-pod direct distribution model [14][20]. Each senior Relationship Manager (RM) is backed by a dedicated pod of Account Managers (AMs), Team Leaders, and Product Specialists [14]. New client families join primarily through existing-client referrals and targeted outreach across Indian Tier-1/Tier-2 cities plus Dubai and UK hubs [3][14].

The engine of this distribution model is RM vintage compounding. An Account Manager spends 2–4 years supporting a senior RM, learning ARWL's portfolio diagnostics and client cadence before promotion [14]. Because RMs are homegrown, ARWL avoids the 30%–40% revenue-share guarantees demanded by lateral hires. Regret RM attrition stays below 1%, and AUM per RM compounds steadily as cohorts mature [3][14]. By FY26, ~401 RMs managed Rs 93,037 Cr across 13,395 client families. That equals ~Rs 232 Cr of AUM per RM and ~33.4 families per RM, matching global best-in-class private client ratios [3][20].

web_blocks.caption: RM Productivity & Cohort Unit Economics (FY22–FY26)
web_blocks.takeaway: AUM per RM more than doubled from ~Rs 112 Cr (FY22) to ~Rs 232 Cr (FY26) while average AUM per family rose from Rs 4.65 Cr to Rs 6.95 Cr, driving powerful operating leverage without branch capex.

web_blocks.caption: FY26 Unit Economics Waterfall (Audited Consolidated P&L & Cash Flow, Rs Cr)
web_blocks.takeaway: On Rs 1,253 Cr of FY26 sales, ARWL converted Rs 586 Cr into operating profit (46.8% OPM) and Rs 397 Cr into net profit (31.7% PAT margin), with Rs 281 Cr in CFO and just Rs 13 Cr in capex (Rs 268 Cr FCF).

web_blocks.caption: Per ₹100 of Revenue Waterfall (FY26 Audited Consolidated)
web_blocks.takeaway: Every Rs 100 of revenue yields Rs 46.8 of operating profit, Rs 31.7 of PAT, and Rs 21.4 of Free Cash Flow; the gap between PAT (Rs 397 Cr) and CFO (Rs 281 Cr) reflects working-capital / receivable and tax timing shifts.

web_blocks.title: Why FY27 Headline Margins Look Lower Than FY26
paragraphs: In Q4 FY26, Q1 FY27, and Q2 FY27, reported OPM dropped from 45%–47% to 29%–34% as Expenses jumped from ~Rs 158–160 Cr/quarter to Rs 203–227 Cr/quarter [1].

This was driven primarily by front-loaded non-cash ESOP accounting charges under the ARWL ESOP-2025 scheme rather than cash commission inflation [10]. Stripping out ESOP charges and investment fair-value gains, H1 FY27 adjusted PAT still grew 23% YoY to Rs 238 Cr [5].

book_paragraphs: Have you ever wondered why most wealth management firms struggle to turn revenue growth into shareholder wealth? In theory, managing rich people's money should be a license to print cash. In practice, the economics often leak out the back door to star Relationship Managers. A bank or boutique poaches a senior private banker with a massive guaranteed bonus, that banker brings over Rs 300 crore of client assets, and three years later a rival poaches the same banker away—taking the clients with them.

Anand Rathi Wealth cracked this code by building a farm system instead of a free-agency market. Walk into their system as a young graduate, and you start as an Account Manager sitting alongside a veteran RM. For two to four years, you learn the exact quantitative pitch, sit in family review meetings, and absorb the firm's culture. Only then do you graduate to become an RM yourself. Look at what that does to unit economics: between FY22 and FY26, the number of RMs grew modestly from ~293 to 401, yet total AUM nearly tripled from Rs 32,906 crore to Rs 93,037 crore. That means AUM per RM more than doubled from Rs 112 crore to Rs 232 crore, while average AUM per client family climbed from Rs 4.65 crore to Rs 6.95 crore.

Now trace ₹100 of FY26 revenue through the business to see how clean this machine really is. Out of every ₹100 of revenue (on a Rs 1,253 crore consolidated top line), Rs 53.23 goes to employee compensation, RM incentives, and office/technology overheads. Zero goes to raw materials or inventory. That leaves Rs 46.77 in operating profit! Subtract Rs 2.71 for depreciation, Rs 1.28 for lease interest, and Rs 11.09 for taxes, and Anand Rathi Wealth drops Rs 31.68 straight to the bottom line as Net Profit.

And how much capital does it need to reinvest to keep growing at 20%+ a year? Almost nothing. Capex in FY26 was just Rs 13 crore—roughly ₹1.04 out of every ₹100 of revenue—leaving Rs 268 crore of Free Cash Flow. That is why the company can pay regular dividends, execute buybacks, and compound ROCE near 59% without touching debt. Still, you and I must keep one eye on the FY27 quarterly P&L: following the ARWL ESOP-2025 grant, non-cash employee stock option charges pushed reported operating margins down from 47% to the 29%–34% range in Mar–Sep 2026. The cash economics remain intact, but headline EPS is temporarily noisier.

book_callouts.title: Narrator's Reflection: The 70%–98% CFO Conversion Nuance
paragraphs: In FY24, CFO was Rs 278 Cr against Rs 226 Cr of PAT (over 120% conversion). In FY26, CFO was Rs 281 Cr against Rs 397 Cr of PAT (70% CFO/EBITDA ratio).

Why did working capital absorb cash in FY26? As we will examine in Chapter 6, Other Assets rose from Rs 530 Cr to Rs 873 Cr as treasury/receivable balances expanded—making cash-flow tracking essential as scale grows.
